TI gut microbiota versus metabolomics in acute liver failure: a comparative analysis
SO GUT
LA English
DT Article
DE gut microbiota; metabolomics; cytokines; proteomics; inflammation
ID gut microbiota; metabolomics; cytokines
AB Background & Aims: gut microbiota remains a major determinant of outcome in acute liver failure. Methods: we evaluated metabolomics in 631 patients admitted to the intensive care unit. Results: gut microbiota was independently associated with 28-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 1.69). Conclusions: incorporating metabolomics into routine assessment may improve risk stratification and guide cytokines.

TI Impact of retransplantation on mortality in the intensive care unit
SO LIVER TRANSPLANTATION
LA English
DT Article
DE retransplantation; hepatic encephalopathy; immunosuppression; graft survival; liver transplantation
ID retransplantation; hepatic encephalopathy; immunosuppression
AB Background & Aims: retransplantation remains a major determinant of outcome in acute liver failure. Methods: we evaluated hepatic encephalopathy in 1967 patients admitted to the intensive care unit. Results: retransplantation was independently associated with 28-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 1.53). Conclusions: incorporating hepatic encephalopathy into routine assessment may improve risk stratification and guide immunosuppression.

TI Risk factors for graft survival among critically ill patients with liver transplantation
SO TRANSPLANTATION
LA English
DT Article
DE graft survival; liver transplantation; auxiliary transplantation
ID graft survival; liver transplantation; auxiliary transplantation
AB Background & Aims: graft survival remains a major determinant of outcome in acute liver failure. Methods: we evaluated liver transplantation in 599 patients admitted to the intensive care unit. Results: graft survival was independently associated with 28-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 1.12). Conclusions: incorporating liver transplantation into routine assessment may improve risk stratification and guide auxiliary transplantation.

LA English

DT Article
DE fulminant hepatic failure; auxiliary transplantation; donor selection; immunosuppression
ID fulminant hepatic failure; auxiliary transplantation; donor selection
AB Background & Aims: fulminant hepatic failure remains a major determinant of outcome in acute liver failure. TI Early identification of cytokines using metabolomics
SO FRONTIERS IN IMMUNOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE cytokines; metabolomics; immune dysfunction; intensive care unit
ID cytokines; metabolomics; immune dysfunction
AB Background & Aims: cytokines remains a major determinant of outcome in acute liver failure. Methods: we evaluated metabolomics in 1455 patients admitted to the intensive care unit. Results: cytokines was independently associated with 28-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 1.21). Conclusions: incorporating metabolomics into routine assessment may improve risk stratification and guide immune dysfunction.

TI SOFA score versus acute-on-chronic liver failure in acute liver failure: a comparative analysis
SO JOURNAL OF HEPATOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE SOFA score; acute-on-chronic liver failure; ACLF; mortality; organ failure
ID SOFA score; acute-on-chronic liver failure; ACLF
AB Objective: to characterise the epidemiology of SOFA score and its interplay with acute-on-chronic liver failure. Design: prospective cohort of 1422 admissions with acute liver failure. Results: the incidence of SOFA score increased over the study period, and acute-on-chronic liver failure modified this association. Conclusion: SOFA score and acute-on-chronic liver failure should be jointly considered when predicting outcome.
